expected_behavior: assigns the variant server-side / at the edge (middleware) and renders the correct HTML, with no client-side DOM swap and no anti-flicker snippet
logs exposure server-side at assignment time (ad blockers drop 10-30% of client events)
persists the assignment in a cookie so a visitor always sees the same variant
recommends the precompute pattern (encode the variant in a URL segment) to keep static CDN caching

cases.prompt: is my test done? it's been running 2 days with 40 conversions per variant
expected_behavior: says no: flags the ~300-conversions-per-variant floor and a >=2-week multi-cycle minimum
warns against peeking / early-stopping and recommends running an A/A test first to validate tooling
notes only ~13% of tests reach a significant winner (directional) and frames the low-traffic reality

cases.prompt: should I use a bandit or an A/B test for my Black Friday promo variants
expected_behavior: recommends a multi-armed bandit (Thompson Sampling) for many short-lived, high-traffic variants to minimize regret
reserves fixed-split A/B for permanent structural decisions needing clean causal certainty
notes bandits need a conversion floor before they route meaningfully (below it they behave like round-robin)

cases.prompt: my landing page gets 200 visitors a week, how do I A/B test it
expected_behavior: flags that this traffic cannot reach significance in a reasonable window
recommends qualitative methods (heatmaps, session replay, user testing, before/after) instead of an underpowered test
explains that piling on tests at low traffic just produces false winners faster
